newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WOODS WINS RAIN-SHORTENED MERCEDES CHAMPIONSHIP IN PLAYOFF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS WINS RAIN-SHORTENED MERCEDES CHAMPIONSHIP IN PLAYOFF.

text.p: Tiger Woods won the season-opening Mercedes Championship with a birdie on the first hole of a sudden death playoff with Tom Lehman after rain washed out the final round on Sunday.

Woods had birdied the last four holes of the third round on Saturday to tie Lehman for the lead at 14-under par. But the 18-hole showdown between the 1996 Rookie of the Year and the 1996 Player of the Year became a one-hole playoff.
The 21-year-old sensation stuck his tee shot within eight inches and tapped in for victory after Lehman had put his tee shot into the lake guarding the green.
"I really wanted to play 18 holes today," said Lehman, the British Open champion. "I was looking forward to going head to head with Tiger."
Woods now has three titles in just nine starts as a professional and the much-publicised $40 million sponsorship deal he received from Nike is beginning to look like a bargain.
"It's a perfect start to the year," said Woods, who picked up $216,000 and a Mercedes-Benz for the win that pushed his career earnings to $1,006,594.
He is by far the fastest ever to crack the $1 million earnings mark. South African Ernie Els was the previous fastest, reaching the milestone in 28 tournaments.
The supremely confident youngster said he was not surprised to have won so much so quickly.
"This is what I set out to do. It's no surprise if you win when you have the mindset that you're going to win from the start of the week."
Only Horton Smith, who won seven times before he was 21, and Gene Sarazen reached three titles at a younger age than the PGA Tour's latest pheneom.
The playoff was staged on the 186 yard par-three seventh hole, the only playable hole on the water-logged course.
Lehman's 6-iron tee shot landed in the lake some four yards from the edge of the green.
"To be honest, the wind fooled me a bit," Lehman said. "Maybe because there was so much mud I teed my ball up too high, anyway, it ballooned up and the wind caught it.
"Tiger hit a great shot, of course he had no pressure on him then, but it was still a great shot," Lehman said.
Woods put his own 6-iron within easy putting distance of the hole.
"I was lucky Tom hit first," Woods admitted. "I didn't know what the wind was doing. I aimed at the middle of the green, playing it kinda safe."
